## §1 - What was tested

The crawl covers the full v1.0 contract surface across the catalog: canonical override correctness, og:url mirroring, schema emission counts, HTTP response codes, dev-theme render integrity. Per Tina's specification, the crawl was run **before** any production publish, against the dev theme, with the cookied admin session.

Per-URL verdict criteria:

- **PASS** - canonical URL matches expected per the 4-branch logic; og:url mirrors canonical; correct schema emission count for the template (Product on PDPs, Article on blog posts, BreadcrumbList on PDPs/collections/articles); HTTP 200; rendered against the dev theme.
- **WARN** - HTTP 200 and dev-rendered, but the URL falls outside the v1.0 contract scope (tag-page surfaces). Remediation noted explicitly.
- **FAIL** - any contract violation. Zero observed.
- **ERROR** - crawler-side exception. Zero observed.

## §3 - The 5 WARN URLs (out-of-contract scope, classified)

All 5 WARNs are tag-page surfaces - URLs Shopify auto-generates when products carry tags. These were not part of the v1.0 milestone contract (which covers Product, Collection, Blog post, Blog index template canonical and schema work). They are HTTP-200 reachable and dev-rendered cleanly; the WARN flag is an observation that the catalog has tag-page indexable surfaces that v1.0 deliberately did not address.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `https://lammeuld.dk/collections/alle-lamper/products/wall-lamp-celia-white` | tag_page_indexable | Out-of-contract tag page | `noindex,follow` gated on `current_tags != blank` (separate engagement) |

| 5 | `https://lammeuld.dk/collections/tv-borde/500-1000-kr` | tag_page_indexable | Out-of-contract tag page | Same as #1 |

## §5 - Validity guarantees

The crawl meets each of the following integrity guarantees:

1. **No URL caused a crawler-side exception.** `errored = 0`. Every URL returned a response the crawler could parse and verdict.
2. **No URL needed a retry.** `retried = 0`. First-attempt response was conclusive on every URL.
3. **No URL leaked to the live theme.** `live_fallback = 0`. The cookied session held for all 500 URLs; every render was against the dev theme.
4. **The cookie did not expire mid-crawl.** Captured separately as `cookie_fresh_post_crawl = true` in the underlying crawl data.
5. **Sentinel URLs gave consistent verdicts at start and end of the crawl.** Five sentinel URLs (one per major template type: PDP, Collection, Paginated collection, Blog post, Blog index) were re-tested at crawl-end and matched their start-of-crawl verdict. `sentinel_drift = false` confirms no environmental change occurred during the crawl window.
6. **Per-template strict-pass = 100% across all in-contract templates.** The 5 WARNs are confined to the out-of-contract `collection_tag` template type.

## §6 - How to reproduce

The crawl harness is a Python script using `httpx` async with a captured admin session cookie. Methodology:

1. **URL pool construction** - the catalog is enumerated via Shopify's product / collection / blog feeds plus a curated set of static pages, paginated collection variants, tag-URL exemplars, and the 5 Layer A sentinel URLs.
2. **Cookied session** - the crawler holds the admin session cookie that surfaces the dev theme at the storefront edge (per Shopify's preview mechanism). Without the cookie, `?preview_theme_id=` alone returns the live theme.
3. **Per-URL verdict** - canonical URL extracted from `<link rel="canonical">`, og:url from the Open Graph meta tags, JSON-LD count and types from `<script type="application/ld+json">` blocks, HTTP status from the response code. Each is checked against the 4-branch logic and per-template expected emission count.
4. **Sentinel monitoring** - the 5 sentinel URLs are crawled at start, mid, and end of the run; if their verdicts drift, the crawl is invalidated and re-run. Drift was zero in this run.

The script and the per-URL crawl results are retained on the engineer side. They can be made available for re-validation on request.

The dev theme is in a state where every contracted surface canonicalizes correctly, emits the contracted schema correctly, and renders cleanly. The 500-URL pre-publish validation that Tina requested in the milestone scope is complete and clean.

The five WARN observations are not blockers for live publish - they are out-of-contract surfaces. After live publish, a post-publish 500-URL crawl will run against the live URLs (no `?preview_theme_id=` parameter; live state) and the same validation criteria will be re-applied. Expected outcome: 100% strict-pass rate carries over, with the same five WARN observations for tag-page surfaces.

That post-publish crawl is part of the contracted 30-day monitoring window (deliverable per Tina's scope: *"Post-publish 500-URL crawl confirming canonical spec matches live reality"*) and runs after Vadim's manual publish click.
